title: Speed and correctness of a comparison

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Per this page, how do `==` and `equals()` compare in speed, and which one should compare String contents?

options.text: equals() is the faster one, and == is the one for contents
options.says: The page says == is generally faster, and that equals() is the one that compares content.

options.text: == is the faster one, and equals() is the one for contents
options.says: The page says == only compares addresses and is faster, but equals() should be preferred for content.

options.text: Both are equally fast, and either one works for contents
options.says: The page says == compares references, not content, so it does not work for contents.

questions.stem: Per this page, why is `equalsIgnoreCase()` better than lower-casing both Strings and then calling `equals()`?

options.text: It treats a null String as equal to an empty one
options.says: The page says nothing of null here; equalsIgnoreCase only ignores case.

options.text: It ignores the spaces at either end of each String
options.says: The page says equalsIgnoreCase ignores case; spaces still count.

options.text: It avoids creating new String objects to compare
options.says: The page says equalsIgnoreCase is more efficient because it avoids creating new String objects.

concepts: equalsIgnoreCase avoids creating the new Strings that lower-casing both sides would.
== is faster than equals(), but equals() is the one that compares content, and correctness comes first.
